problem: End-to-end ALFRED agents rely on a shallow understanding of language instructions and miss semantic relationships, such as an object being inside a closed container (fridge, drawer), which makes long-horizon embodied instruction following inefficient and error-prone in unseen scenes.
motivation: EIF tasks need accurate visual perception together with deep language understanding for task scheduling. Objects hidden in closed containers require the agent to infer that a container must be opened, and a modular design can add this reasoning and make search more efficient.
key_idea: REIF is a modular framework (visual perception, language understanding, semantic search, closed-container prediction, navigation, operation) that uses language-derived semantics to predict closed containers and search objects efficiently in ALFRED.
insight: From the abstract alone, the claimed gains come from the semantic search module (more efficient object search) and the closed-container prediction module (deeper language understanding). No ablations are available in the provided text, so these attributions are unverified.
method: Visual perception: perceives the scene visually to detect objects and features (details not given in the abstract).
Language understanding: uses a large language model to parse instructions into task structure and semantic relations.
Semantic search: supports more efficient search for target objects.
Closed container prediction: infers whether the target object is inside a closed container so that the agent opens it.
Navigation: moves the agent toward the searched target or container.
Operation: executes interaction actions on the target object, including objects inside closed containers.

setting.backbone: LLM plus vision-language multimodal modules (specific models not stated in the abstract)
setting.training_data: ALFRED task instructions (details not given in the abstract)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (assumed for ALFRED; not stated in the abstract)
setting.action_space: ALFRED high-level and low-level actions (navigation and object interaction)

results: The abstract reports state-of-the-art unseen-scene performance on ALFRED, with 50.83% accuracy and 23.06% efficiency, and first place on the ALFRED leaderboard at the time. Baselines and margins are not given.

Performance is reported only under certain step-length limits and only in the ALFRED simulator, with no real-robot validation.
